This avoids the use by the parties of capital leases , consulting fees , and other non-traditional forms of payment to lower the figure against which the commission amount is applied . I have been involved in a number of deals which use that concept and , while it requires some attention to the manner in which the term is defined , I think it can work fine for the purchaser . If defined appropriately , the term ought to result in exactly the same commission figure as would result from use of a more traditional concept of consideration . As for percentages for success fees , the numbers range pretty widely depending on the industry group , the expertise of the consultant , the size of the deal and the anticipated amount of work . I have NUM transaction in the works with an anticipated price of $ NUM , in which the fee is a graduated fee of NUM % for the NUM $ NUM , NUM % for the next $ NUM , and NUM % thereafter . Most deals include a minimum compensation figure designed to protect the consultant against an unusually small price . I have never been big on paying retainers or monthly fees , but many consultants require them in order to defer costs . As lot of my effort in negotiating these goes into determining when the fee is earned . If a deal closes during the term of the agreement , there is usually no disagreement , but when there is a " tail " provision which entitles the consultant to the fee after the agreement has expired , there can be a dispute over whether a prospect was really a prospect . < URL > < URL > Utah Federal Court Vacated Foreclosure Injunction on Federal Preemption On June NUM , NUM , the U.S. District Court for the District of Utah released a memorandum in support of its decision to vacate a state court order granting a preliminary injunction against Bank of America and its foreclosure subsidiary , ReconTrust Company , N.A. in the case of Cox v. ReconTrust Company , N.A. The NUM District Court of Utah prohibited ReconTrust and Bank of America from pursuing all foreclosure sales in Utah while it determined whether ReconTrust and Bank of America were authorized to do business in the state . The federal district court overturned that order on June NUM , NUM , and released the supporting memorandum NUM week later . In the memorandum , the federal court NUM addressed the threshold issue of jurisdiction and explained that it has jurisdiction to hear the case based on the doctrine of complete preemption . Cox amended her complaint to remove a Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act to eliminate federal question jurisdiction . Even so , the court determined that the doctrine of complete preemption applied to Cox 's remaining complaints that ReconTrust failed to register as a foreign corporation in Utah and could not serve as a trustee in the foreclosure sales . Because federal law completely preempted Cox 's claims , the court held deemed the lawsuit essentially federal in nature so as to render federal jurisdiction appropriate . With respect to Cox 's claim under the foreign corporation statute , the court determined that Congress intended the National Bank Act to exclusively govern the issue of where a national bank is authorized to transact business , as evidenced in NUM U.S.C. Â § Â § NUM , NUM , NUM . As such , Utah 's foreign corporation registration requirement is completely preempted by the National Bank Act . Turning to ReconTrust 's ability to act as a trustee , the court noted that Utah law allows only certain depository institutions , not including national banks , to act as trustees . However , the court cited a National Bank Act provision , NUM U.S.C. Â § 92a ( a ) , that gives the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency authority to allow national banks to act as trustees whenever a state allows a competitor of a national bank to act as a trustee , as is the case under the Utah statute . The court concluded that removal of the lawsuit to federal court was appropriate because federal law exclusively governed Cox 's claims pertaining to ReconTrust 's authority to conduct business as a foreign corporation and to act as a trustee . After determining that it had jurisdiction to hear the case , the federal court vacated the state court 's order halting all foreclosure sales by ReconTrust and Bank of America in Utah . The court explained that Cox had no standing to seek an injunction against all foreclosure sales in the state of Utah - she could only properly seek an injunction with respect to her own foreclosure . Further , the federal court found that the state court improperly granted the injunction without a hearing to give ReconTrust or Bank of America an opportunity to be heard . Finally , the court deemed the injunction improper because , as noted above , the National Bank Act preempted all the claims .
